sol_lobbying.title: Statutes of limitation for child sexual abuse, and the lobbying against reform
summary_facts: The US Catholic Church spent about $10.6 million lobbying in eight northeastern states from 2011 to 2018, including against limitation-period reform: Pennsylvania $5,322,979; New York $2,912,772; Connecticut $875,261; New Jersey $633,458; Massachusetts $537,551; New Hampshire $134,345; Maine $124,260; Rhode Island $61,961 (report 'Church Influencing State', commissioned by four law firms representing survivors, from public lobbying filings, reported by NBC News June 2019).

In Pennsylvania the Catholic Conference spent over $7.6 million on lobbying from 2014 to 2024 and the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania nearly $20.7 million (both lobby on other issues too); as of February 2025 Pennsylvania still had no revival window, after a 2021 constitutional amendment failed because the state did not advertise it (Spotlight PA).

The Boy Scouts of America's national organization spent about $2.5 million on lobbying from 2011 to 2017, and the Scouts and a local council spent $486,505 lobbying in Pennsylvania from 2016 to 2018 (USA TODAY / Arizona Republic / Center for Public Integrity, 2019).

In 2017 the American Insurance Association spent $130,000 lobbying New York on issues including the Child Victims Act; AIA, Liberty Mutual and Zurich together spent more than $375,000 lobbying Albany that year (NBC New York I-Team, 29 March 2018).

Child USA counts 33 US jurisdictions (30 states, DC and two territories) that have passed revival windows or revival laws for child sexual abuse claims since 2002; Colorado's, Kentucky's and Utah's were later held unconstitutional.
New York's one-year window (opened 14 August 2019, extended twice to 14 August 2021) produced more than 9,000 lawsuits (AP, August 2021).

Maryland removed its limitation period for child sexual abuse claims in 2023; after more than 3,100 suits, the legislature in 2025 cut damage caps from $1.5m to $700,000 for private institutions and from $890,000 to $400,000 for public ones, effective 1 June 2025 (Maryland Matters).

All Australian states and territories removed limitation periods for child sexual abuse civil claims between 2015 (Victoria) and 2018 (Western Australia, South Australia, Queensland), following the Royal Commission's 2015 Redress and Civil Litigation report.

England and Wales removed the three-year limitation period for child sexual abuse personal-injury claims through section 96 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026, in force 29 June 2026; Scotland had done so in 2017.

bankruptcy_shield.title: Bankruptcy and asset transfers as a shield against abuse claims
summary_facts: Since the Archdiocese of Portland's first filing on 6 July 2004, more than 40 US Catholic dioceses and religious orders have filed for Chapter 11; Rochester's 2019 filing was the 20th diocese — half of all filings came after the 2019 wave of revival windows (Wikipedia, diocesan articles).

Filings often came just before a trial or deposition: Portland (hours before two trials, 2004), San Diego (hours before the first of ~150 suits, 2007), Wilmington (the day before trial, 2009), Milwaukee (two days before the archbishop's deposition, 2011), Baltimore (two days before Maryland's Child Victims Act took effect, 2023).

Boy Scouts of America: filed 18 February 2020; more than 82,000 abuse claims; $2.46 billion plan confirmed 8 September 2022 with third-party releases for local councils, insurers and churches; Third Circuit upheld May 2025; US Supreme Court denied review 12 January 2026.

In Harrington v. Purdue Pharma (27 June 2024), the US Supreme Court held the Bankruptcy Code does not allow non-consensual releases of claims against non-debtor third parties — the device diocesan plans have used to protect parishes, schools and insurers. The BSA plan survived because it was already 'substantially consummated'.

In 2007 Archbishop Timothy Dolan asked the Vatican to move $57 million into a Milwaukee cemetery trust for 'improved protection of these funds from any legal claim and liability'; the Vatican approved it five weeks later (documents released in bankruptcy, July 2013).
Archdiocese of Santa Fe transferred assets worth over $150 million into trusts and incorporated parishes before filing; in October 2020 the judge let survivors pursue fraudulent-transfer claims.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Portland (Oregon)
rows.note: First US Catholic diocese to file (6 July 2004), hours before two abuse trials; argued parish assets were not archdiocesan assets. Paid $71.45m to 169 victims (2007 plan).

rows.name: Diocese of Tucson
rows.note: Filed Sept 2004; $22.2m settlement approved June 2005.

rows.name: Diocese of Spokane
rows.note: Filed Dec 2004; agreed to pay at least $48m.

rows.name: Diocese of Davenport
rows.note: Filed 10 Oct 2006; by Nov 2007 court allocated $37m to 156 victims; sold bishop's residence.

rows.name: Diocese of San Diego (1st filing)
rows.note: Filed 27 Feb 2007 hours before the first of ~150 lawsuits was heard; Sept 2007 settled 144 claims for $198.1m.

rows.name: Diocese of Fairbanks
rows.note: Filed March 2008; ~140 plaintiffs, many Alaska Native, abused by priests and church workers since the 1950s; co-defendant Jesuit Oregon Province settled for $50m.

rows.name: Jesuits — Oregon Province
rows.note: Filed Feb 2009; agreed in 2011 to pay $166m to abuse victims (many Native American in Alaska and the Northwest).

rows.name: Diocese of Wilmington
rows.note: Filed 18 Oct 2009, the day before the first trial, after Delaware's 2007 window; 2011 plan paid 150 victims $77.425m.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Milwaukee
rows.note: Filed 4 Jan 2011, two days before the archbishop's deposition. Documents released in bankruptcy (July 2013) showed Archbishop Timothy Dolan in 2007 asked the Vatican to move $57m into a cemetery trust for "improved protection of these funds from any legal claim and liability"; the Vatican approved five weeks later.

rows.name: Congregation of Christian Brothers (North America)
rows.note: Filed 2011; 2013 agreed ~$16.5m to more than 400 people abused as children (incl. Mount Cashel, Newfoundland, claimants).

rows.name: Diocese of Gallup
rows.note: Filed 12 Nov 2013; by Feb 2017 had paid >$17.6m to 57 victims.

rows.name: Diocese of Helena
rows.note: Filed Jan 2014 as part of a $15m settlement for 362 victims.

rows.name: Diocese of Stockton
rows.note: Filed 2014; plan approved 2017, ~$15m to over two dozen victims.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Saint Paul and Minneapolis
rows.note: Filed 16-17 Jan 2015 after Minnesota's 2013 window; $210m settlement (2018) — $170m from insurers, $40m from archdiocese and parishes.

rows.name: Diocese of Duluth
rows.note: Filed 7 Dec 2015 after an $8m jury verdict; May 2019 agreed $40m to 125 plaintiffs.

rows.name: Diocese of New Ulm
rows.note: Filed 3 March 2017; made Minnesota the first state with three Catholic diocesan bankruptcies.

rows.name: Diocese of Great Falls-Billings
rows.note: Filed March 2017 weeks before first trials; $20m to 86 victims; critics alleged the diocese moved ~$16m of assets into an entity it controlled (CASC).

rows.name: Crosier Fathers and Brothers
rows.note: Order filed 2017 after agreeing to pay $25.5m.

rows.name: Diocese of Winona-Rochester
rows.note: Filed Dec 2018 over 121 lawsuits; Feb 2021 $21.5m to 145 victims.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Agaña (Guam)
rows.note: Filed 15-16 Jan 2019 after Guam's 2016 permanent window; claims rose to nearly 280; Jan 2020 plan offered $21m; sold Yona property for $6.1m. Former Archbishop Anthony Apuron found guilty in a canonical trial (2018-19).

rows.name: Diocese of Saint Cloud
rows.note: Filed June 2020; $22.5m for 70 survivors; plan approved Dec 2020.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Santa Fe
rows.note: Filed Dec 2018 (announced Nov 2018); 395 claimants. Before filing it transferred assets worth over $150m into trusts and incorporated parishes; in Oct 2020 the bankruptcy judge allowed survivors to sue alleging these were fraudulent transfers.

rows.name: Diocese of Rochester
rows.note: Filed 12 Sept 2019, first NY diocese and 20th US diocese to file, after NY Child Victims Act window.

rows.name: Diocese of Harrisburg
rows.note: Filed 19 Feb 2020 (first in Pennsylvania), >200 creditors, liabilities $50-100m, assets <$10m.

rows.name: Boy Scouts of America
rows.note: Filed 18 Feb 2020 in Delaware; >82,000 claims by 16 Nov 2020 bar date; $2.46bn plan confirmed 8 Sept 2022 with third-party releases for local councils, insurers and chartered organisations (churches); upheld by Third Circuit May 2025; Supreme Court denied certiorari 12 Jan 2026. ~$295.5m paid to >36,000 survivors by late 2025; trust estimates full value >$7bn and billed non-settling insurers.

rows.name: Diocese of Buffalo
rows.note: Filed 28 Feb 2020 acknowledging >500 claims; agreed March 2024 to sell 22+ properties incl. HQ for $9.8m. Leaked audio showed Bishop Malone diverted 40% of Catholic Charities donations to a separate foundation shielded from suits.

rows.name: Archdiocese of New Orleans
rows.note: Filed 1 May 2020 with >500 claims (after a Dec 2019 approved settlement of at least $230m with hundreds of survivors per Wikipedia main article); continued paying retirement benefits to abusers until the bankruptcy judge ordered it to stop.

rows.name: Diocese of Syracuse
rows.note: Filed June 2020; 38 new CVA suits filed days before.

rows.name: Diocese of Rockville Centre
rows.note: Filed Oct 2020 (4th NY diocese). April 2024 $200m offer rejected by 86% of survivors; Sept 2024 agreed $323m for 530 victims ($85.3m from insurance). Its parishes declared bankruptcy so insurers could buy back policies.

rows.name: Diocese of Camden
rows.note: Filed Oct 2020 after NJ window; April 2022 agreed $87.5m.

rows.name: Diocese of Norwich
rows.note: Filed July 2021; plan with $31m trust (proposed Feb 2025) for victims incl. Mount Saint John school; exited May 2025.

rows.name: Diocese of Santa Rosa
rows.note: Filed March 2023 facing nearly 200 suits under California AB 218.

rows.name: Diocese of Albany
rows.note: Filed March 2023 facing CVA suits.

rows.name: Diocese of Oakland
rows.note: Filed May 2023 citing 330 suits since 2020.

rows.name: Diocese of Ogdensburg
rows.note: Filed July 2023.

rows.name: Archdiocese of San Francisco
rows.note: Filed Aug 2023, ~500 suits.

rows.name: Archdiocese of Baltimore
rows.note: Filed 29 Sept 2023, two days before Maryland CVA took effect (1 Oct 2023); Maryland AG 2023 report identified >600 victims over 80 years; survivors moved to dismiss the case (Sept 2025).

rows.name: Diocese of Sacramento
rows.note: Filed 1 April 2024 amid >250 suits.

rows.name: Diocese of San Diego (2nd filing)
rows.note: Second filing 17 June 2024.

rows.name: Diocese of Burlington
rows.note: Filed 30 Sept 2024 after Vermont's 2019 permanent window.

rows.name: Diocese of Fresno
rows.note: Filed July 2025, 153 suits.

rows.name: USA Gymnastics
rows.note: Filed Dec 2018, a month after the USOPC began decertification; $380m settlement with Nassar survivors (Dec 2021, NYT); USAG and two related organisations settled for nearly $900m in total incl. Michigan State $500m to 332 victims (2018).
